text:
sasha: heads up — 19:50 release 2026-03-17 started showing a perf regression in the runtime. P50 latency up ~2.3x and compile-queue spiked on dedicated pools.
ci-bot: alert: perf-check failed on merge 6f2a1bc — kernel-autopick score drift detected; compile storm detected (peak 420 queued compiles).
mike: observed same. KV cache eviction rate jumped at the same time, lots of cold-loads hitting compile. Suspect an autotune pick flip that chooses a slower kernel for short-seq batches.
anya: throwing up a flamegraph + timeline: https://s3.redwood-ci/internal/flame/1799123456.png — you can see back-to-back JITs for the same op across nodes. Also attaching runtime logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-17T19:50:12Z] compile_request op=matmul shape=[1,1024,1024] profile_id=auto_2026_03_17
[2026-03-17T19:50:12Z] kernel_pick: policy=autopick chosen=matmul_f32_fast fallback=matmul_f32_vector
[2026-03-17T19:50:12Z] compile_start nid=ip-10-0-1-23
[2026-03-17T19:50:13Z] compile_error: cache_miss=true, compile_time=0.92s
```
kevin: which commit range did CI signal? ci-bot pointed at 6f2a1bc -> 6f2a1bc is the autotune config churn PR by infra team.
sasha: yeah that PR adjusted late-bind thresholds for kernel scoring. When low-batch short-seq hits, it now prefers a higher-throughput kernel that performs worse for tiny batches — explains latency jump.
mike: can we reproduce locally with the short-seq workload? I have a small repro script: ```
# repro short sequence
python -c 'import requests; print(requests.post("http://local:8080/generate", json={"model":"gpt-small","input_len":16,"batch":1}).status_code)'
```
anya: repro confirmed on my devbox — triggered the same compile churn. Profiling shows the autotuner scoring function picked a kernel with a higher steady-state throughput but much larger per-compile binary size, causing compile cache thrash.
lee: quick mitigation: we can disable runtime.autopick for short_batch=true in prod config and roll a hotfix. That should force the previous heuristic until we patch the scorer.
kevin: +1 to hotfix. Also recommend bisecting autotune changes to find the exact line. I'll run a git bisect against infra/autotune and link results.
ci-bot: bisect job started: job_id=b-1799123700 — running on a small fleet.
mike: while bisect runs, let's also add a temporary guard to KV cache so we don't evict entries for recently compiled kernels for 10m. That could dampen storm effect.
sasha: good idea. Can someone prepare a quick changelist? We should aim to push hotfix within the hour. This is blocking the rollout.
anya: opened PR: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/+/PR-4823 (disable autopick short_batch + kv grace) — includes unit tests and a config flag.
kevin: bisect finished — culprit commit is 6f2a1bc: 'autotune: prefer high-throughput kernels at low-latency threshold' — reproducer attached.
lee: rolling out hotfix to canary now. deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/runtime-hotfix-4823 -> 3 nodes.
deploy-bot: deploy success: canary/runtime-hotfix-4823 -> all checks green.
mike: canary metrics look good: compile queue down 87%, p50 latency back to baseline.
sasha: great. who's doing the postmortem? We need a changelog entry and follow-up to improve the scoring model (score should include compile cost and cache pressure).
kevin: I'll take the postmortem, will propose a new scoring metric that includes compile_time_estimate and cache_hotness. Filing issue INF-1290.
sasha: thanks — next steps: revert autotune change or harden scorer? we can revert or add a guard that keeps legacy kernel picks for <32 token sequences while we refine.
kevin: small revert off the PR is safer for now. I'll open a revert PR and schedule rollback window.
anya: leaving logs & profiling in infra bucket for the postmortem: s3://redwood-prod/perf/1799123456/.
lee: tagging SRE to monitor: @oncall-sre — please watch compile queue and KV evictions for the next 6 hours.
ci-bot: perf-check cleared on canary after hotfix.
sasha: ok closing this thread — thanks team. Follow-up in INF-1290 and PM notes. :thumbsup:
